Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 07:12:00 -0400
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes for APAC — possible region routing issue

Hi Tessa,

We started seeing a sustained increase in p95 and p99 latency for calls to the Hosted API that serve our APAC users around 02:00 UTC today. The spike correlates with a rise in RTT and a few 504s during heavy periods. Our telemetry shows many requests appear to be egressing via EU hops instead of the APAC edge.

Attached are traces and a histogram summary. Can your team confirm if there was any routing/fallthrough change this morning that could explain APAC traffic transiting EU? This is impacting our peak SLAs and we need an ETA for mitigation — happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Samir
CTO, Lumina Health

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 07:41:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes for APAC — possible region routing issue

Team — quick update from the infra side after 20m of looking:

- We observed an automated failover policy that was intended for a narrow set of EU peering flaps picked up APAC-origin sessions because a recently merged affinity rule matched a CIDR that overlays our APAC ASN. In short: APAC traffic is being classified as eligible for EU fallback.
- This caused an extra ~150-220ms median RTT for those requests and a higher tail (p95+p99).
- No model-serving nodes are down; this is purely a pathing/egress selection problem.

Immediate actions proposed:
1) Revert the affinity rule merge (route_policy_diff.txt attached) — quick rollback within 10m.
2) Temporarily pin Lumina to APAC-only egress via explicit customer routing (config change) — <10m after rollback.
3) Post-rollback: add unit tests for CIDR overlap and a canary that verifies egress region classification for high-volume customers.

If Tessa wants, I'll open an exec note once we have rollback progress.

—Jonas
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime

Also, we'll temporarily pin your account to APAC egress until the fix is validated. Sorry again for the disruption — I'll follow up with timings.

—Tessa

Subject: Exec brief: APAC-tailed p95 spike resolved — routing policy misclassification

Team — quick exec summary to close the loop. TL;DR: Lumina Health saw a p95/p99 spike on 2026-10-20 starting ~02:00 UTC due to APAC-origin traffic being routed through EU because of a CIDR overlap introduced by a recent affinity-rule merge. Impact: elevated RTT leading to intermittent timeouts for a subset of APAC requests.

What we did:
- Identified misclassification and rolled back the rule at 07:58 UTC; p95 improved to ~210ms (baseline ~180ms).
- Pinned Lumina to APAC egress while we harden routing tests.
- Owners: Karthik (preventive rules/test), Jonas (routing rollback/runbook), Marissa (ops runbook + customer credits), Tessa (customer comms & postmortem).

Risk & mitigation: This is a policy classification risk — not infra capacity. We'll add automated checks for CIDR overlaps and a canary that validates geo-egress for top 20 customers. Target completion: 2 weeks.

Customer remedy: offered Lumina a 3-day credit and an assistance session to tune routing for their traffic profile; Samir accepted the offer and appreciated the speed of the rollback.

Action items:
- Karthik: deliver unit tests + deploy new check (due 2026-11-03).
- Jonas: update rollback playbook and add a pre-merge egress-scope test (due 2026-10-27).
- Marissa: finalize customer credits and legal sign-off (due 2026-10-25).
- Tessa: publish customer-facing summary and internal postmortem (due 2026-10-22).

I'll attach the postmortem to the Jira ticket once complete.

—Tessa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
